concepts.def: Doing what is morally right in business
Corporate Social Responsibility — duty beyond profit
Buying from suppliers who treat workers fairly
Producers paid a fair wage for their goods
Anyone affected by the firm's decisions
Giving up one benefit to gain another

walkthroughs.body_html:
Acting ethically means doing what is morally right — even when it isn't legally required.

It covers honesty in advertising, paying suppliers on time, and treating staff fairly.

CSR is the wider duty to society and the planet.

Examples: paying living wages, sourcing fair-trade ingredients, reducing emissions, supporting communities.

Ethical choices often raise costs: pricier suppliers, slower expansion, more reporting.

But they can boost brand image, customer loyalty and staff motivation — paying back over time.
